tests.title: Display switcher offers List, Tech View and Board View and marks the active one
tests.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Display Switcher") has two Approved work orders: {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17581), led by {Technician-A}, and {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17582), with no lead technician.
  • The Work Orders page shows List at the start: List is the highlighted button in the display switcher.
  • Developer note kept from the automation engineer (nothing for the tester to do): Dev-layer test — fe-unit. Existing coverage: app/src/components/ts/work-orders/**/DisplayOptionSwitcher.spec.ts:42,65,77
tests.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Look at the display switcher at the right of the toolbar and write down which button is highlighted.
  3. Hover the first button of the display switcher and read its tooltip.
  4. Hover the second button and read its tooltip.
  5. Hover the third button and read its tooltip.
  6. Click Tech View in the display switcher.
  7. Look at which switcher button is highlighted.
  8. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  9. Look at which switcher button is highlighted.
  10. Click List in the display switcher.
  11. Look at which switcher button is highlighted.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: the switcher offers exactly three display options, and List is the highlighted one.
  • Steps 3 to 5: the tooltips read List, Tech View and Board View, in that order.
  • Step 7: only Tech View is highlighted.
  • Step 9: only Board View is highlighted.
  • Step 11: only List is highlighted.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 54 (15 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R1, S1-R9 and S1-R9b, read 15 Oct 2026. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 24, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 15 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.19-72f4f3b (staging) on 10/16/2026.

The design's tooltips read Table, By Lead Tech and Board, and this case used to accept any label. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 24) that the tooltips read List, Tech View and Board View; PRD version 54 says so, and a different word is now a fail.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R1: “The Work Orders toolbar offers List, Tech View, and Board View display options.”
  • S1-R9: “The switcher visually indicates the active display option.”
  • S1-R9b: “The switcher’s hover tooltip opens above the switcher, so it never covers the table’s column header row. The tooltips read List, Tech View and Board View.”

AUTOMATION: READY

tests.title: A user who never chose a display sees List
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 2 users · 1 browser · about 15 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • [User-B]: a brand-new user who has never opened Work Orders, with a role that has Work Orders view (e.g. Service Advisor) and this location picked in Location, and an email you can open.
  • Desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • [Tech-A]: one eligible technician at this location. A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Default List" (used by this case only) with one Approved work order [WO-1] led by [Tech-A].
  • Names are examples; what must hold: [User-B] has never opened Work Orders (so has never chosen a display).

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Check the location in the top bar next to the bell; to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Create everything below in this location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Default List" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Default List": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-702): Lead Technician = [Tech-A].
  6. Create a brand-new user who has never opened Work Orders: Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff > New Staff Member with an email you can open (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Never Chose"), a role with Work Orders view (e.g. Service Advisor), at least one Department (required), with this location picked in Location > Save & Close. Accept the invitation and set a password, but do not open Work Orders as this user. Record this user as [User-B].
  7. Check the setup worked: as [User-A], Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Default List" shows [WO-1]; Settings > Staff lists [User-B] at this location. If [User-B] has already opened Work Orders, create another new user and use that one.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Sign out.
  2. Sign in as [User-B].
  3. Open Work Orders from the top navigation.
  4. Look at the work orders area and the display switcher.
  5. Refresh the page.
  6. Look at the display again.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The page opens in List: the ordinary work order table, not grouped by technician and not shown as columns of cards.
  • In the display switcher the List option is the highlighted one.
  • After the refresh the page is still in List.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S1-R2, Key Decisions, read 8 Oct 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R2: “List is the default display option for every user until they choose another.”
  • Key Decisions: “Default display option remains List. Existing users see no change until they choose otherwise.”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.

tests.title: Switching display keeps the same tab, search, filters and work orders
tests.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-C} (for example Jenny Wilson) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Fibridge") has exactly three Approved work orders: {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17612) led by {Technician-A}, {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17613) led by {Technician-B}, and {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17614) with no lead.
  • Customer {Customer-B} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Fisquare") has one Approved work order, {Work-order-4} (for example S10043-17615), with any lead. {Customer-B}'s name does not contain {Customer-A}'s name, so searching {Customer-A}'s name does not find {Work-order-4}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type the name of {Customer-A}.
  4. Click Status and tick Approved.
  5. Click outside the Status list to close it.
  6. In List, write down every work order number shown.
  7. Click Tech View in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar (tooltip "Tech View").
  8. Write down the work order numbers shown and each group header count.
  9. Click Board View in the display switcher (tooltip "Board View").
  10. Write down the work order numbers on the cards and each column header count.
  11. Click List in the display switcher (tooltip "List").
tests.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 7, 9 and 11: the layout changes straight away on each click, without a page reload.
  • Steps 7 to 11: after every switch the All tab is still selected, the search box still shows the name of {Customer-A}, and Status still shows Approved ticked.
  • Steps 6, 8 and 10: the same work orders appear in all three displays. List shows 3 rows ({Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}), Tech View shows the same 3 (Unassigned 1 + {Technician-A} 1 + {Technician-B} 1 = 3) and Board View shows the same 3 cards. {Work-order-4} appears in none of them.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 52 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R3 and Feature Overview (its filter sentence was reworded in version 52 to name the Technician filter as the second exception, after Imported; this case uses no Technician filter, so the expected results are unchanged), read 14 Oct 2026. Source-verified 14 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R3: “Switching display options immediately re-lays out the current results without changing the filter view, search text, or filters.”
  • Feature Overview: “The existing filter views (the tabs on the left — All, Work Orders, Estimates, Completed) and the filter bar (search, status, assigned to me, and so on) apply the same way in every display option.”
  • Feature Overview (the two exceptions): “Imported work orders are one exception: they open in List only (S1-R13a, S1-R13b). The Technician filter is the other: Tech View and Board View offer it and List does not (S1-R15).”

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 61 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R8, read 16 Oct 2026. Review Decisions 853901313 FF-3 / DR-6. SV-11416 asked the product owner what happens when a lead technician is deleted; the spec covered only a deactivated lead. PRD version 59 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling on Slavcho Mitrov's question on SV-11416) added S3-R20e: such work orders sit under "Deleted technician" with the inactive marker and no grip, take no drops, can be dragged out, and List shows the lead blank (version 68 changed this to "Unassigned"). In versions 66 to 68 (19 Oct 2026) the message after a lead change became "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}", with Undo (step 10). This case follows version 59 and later (was: no "Unknown Technician" column, the header naming the technician as List does).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R20e: “Work orders whose lead technician was deleted in Settings → Staff (the name no longer exists) sit in one column on Board View and one group in Tech View labeled “Deleted technician”, with the inactive marker and no drag grip. Work orders can be dragged out of it; nothing can be dropped onto it. List shows “Unassigned” in the Lead Technician column for these work orders, as today.”
  • S4-N5: “Nothing can be dropped onto the column/group of an inactive technician (S2-N2, S3-N2) or of a technician who is not enrolled at this location (S3-R20c).”
  • S3-N4: “Show an inactive indicator on deactivated technician columns.”
  • S2-N3: “Indicate deactivated technicians as inactive in group headers.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”

  • [Tech-B]: a second eligible technician at this location (same rules as [Tech-A]). Their column shows on Board View and their group in Tech View even with no work orders, so the locked work orders can be dragged over it.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" (used by this case only), with a contact, and two work orders with Lead Technician [Tech-A] set before invoicing: [WO-1] Invoiced and [WO-2] Paid.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard) and [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. How to reach each status (standard steps): Estimate = a new work order whose lines are not approved. Approved = approve its lines. In Progress = a technician clicks Start time clock on an approved line's Labor row. Review = set the work order to Ready for Review with its status control. Complete = enter a tech story on every line, complete each line, then complete the work order. Invoiced = Finance tab > Create Invoice (the work order needs a contact person). Paid = record a full payment on that invoice. Declined = decline the estimate.
  6. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Assign lead technician > click the technician; it is assigned at once.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-511): Lead Technician = [Tech-A], then taken to Invoiced.
    • [WO-2] (e.g. S1-366): Lead Technician = [Tech-A], then taken to Paid.

tests.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" in Search.
  3. Look at the [WO-1] card and write down any sign that it can only be reordered within its technician (e.g. a lock icon).
  4. Hover the lock icon on the [WO-1] card and read its tooltip.
  5. Hover the card, click More actions and hover the Reassign lead technician action.
  6. Read the tooltip shown next to the Reassign lead technician action.
  7. Hover the Unassign action and read its tooltip.
  8. Press Escape to close the menu.
  9. Drag the [WO-1] card over [Tech-B]'s column and, without releasing it, read the note at the top of [Tech-B]'s column.
  10. Release the card and read which column it is in.
  11. Repeat steps 3 to 10 for [WO-2].
  12. Repeat steps 3 to 11 in Tech View on the rows, dragging each row over [Tech-B]'s group.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Invoiced and Paid cards and rows carry a lock icon, the visible sign that they can only be reordered within their current technician and not moved to another one.
  • Hovering the lock icon shows the tooltip “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-1] and “Paid · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-2].
  • Reassign lead technician and Unassign are shown disabled, and their tooltip reads exactly: Invoiced · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-1]) or Paid · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-2]). (A straight or curly apostrophe is not a difference.)
  • While [WO-1] or [WO-2] is dragged over [Tech-B]'s column or group, the note at its top reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-1]) or “Paid · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-2]).

PRD §9 User Feedback Summary row "Reassignment not allowed in current status". Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html): lock icon next to the number with tooltip "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" and a locked menu note; since PRD version 68 the PRD uses the same words, and the PRD text is asserted here. tests.title: Clear shifts removes only the old lead's whole-work-order shifts
tests.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)


Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and Schedule access, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-C} (for example Dana Ortiz) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Clear Shifts Scope") is used by this case only.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17581) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has two approved lines, {Line-1} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and {Line-2} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch").
  • Approved work order {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17582) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has two approved lines, {Line-3} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and {Line-4} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch").
  • Approved work order {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17583) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has two approved lines (for example "Service - Full grease service" and "Service - Adjust clutch").
  • {Work-order-1} has three shifts tomorrow: {Technician-A} 8:00–12:00 covering the entire work order, {Technician-A} 13:00–15:00 on {Line-1} only, and {Technician-C} 8:00–10:00 covering the entire work order.
  • {Work-order-2} has two shifts tomorrow: {Technician-A} 8:00–12:00 covering the entire work order, and {Technician-A} 13:00–15:00 on {Line-3} only.
  • {Work-order-3} has one shift the day after tomorrow: {Technician-A} 8:00–12:00 covering the entire work order.
  • On the Work Orders page, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip).
tests.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Drag {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
  4. Read the question that opens.
  5. Click Clear shifts.
  6. Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
  7. In the question that opens, click Keep shifts.
  8. Click Schedule in the top menu.
  9. Use the arrow next to Today to go to tomorrow.
  10. Read every shift on {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2}.
  11. Use the arrow again to go to the day after tomorrow.
  12. Read the shift on {Work-order-3}.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 4 and 7: both drags open the question "Clear {Technician-A}'s scheduled shifts?" (with the example name: "Clear Esther Howard's scheduled shifts?").
  • Step 5: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column.
  • Step 10: on {Work-order-1}, {Technician-A}'s 8:00–12:00 shift covering the entire work order is gone, and {Technician-C}'s 8:00–10:00 shift is still there.
  • Step 12: {Technician-A}'s 8:00–12:00 shift on {Work-order-3} is still there, unchanged.
  • Steps 7 and 10: {Work-order-2} is now in {Technician-B}'s column, and both of {Technician-A}'s shifts on it (8:00–12:00 and 13:00–15:00) are still there.
  • Step 10: {Technician-A}'s 13:00–15:00 shifts on {Line-1} of {Work-order-1} and on {Line-3} of {Work-order-2} are still there: the question never clears a shift on only some lines.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 49 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R11, S4-R22, S4-R23, S4-R24, S4-R28 (reworded in version 49 on 14 Oct 2026 from Chris Ward's answer 1 of 14 Oct 2026: a work-order-level shift is one that covers every approved line, judged at the moment the lead changes; first defined in version 47 after SV-11126) and S4-R29, read 14 Oct 2026. Review Decisions DR-31 (optional whole-work-order shift clearing). Schedule shift window labels "Entire work order" / "Choose lines" from the Schedule suite. Each work order has two lines so that the 13:00–15:00 shift covers only some of them. On a one-line work order a shift on that line counts (version 49, S4-R28). Source-verified 14 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R11: “When changing the lead technician in Board View or Tech View, ask whether to clear the outgoing lead’s work-order-level scheduled shifts.”
  • S4-R29: “The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.”
  • S4-R22: “If the user chooses to clear shifts, remove only the outgoing lead’s shifts scheduled against that whole work order.”
  • S4-R23: “If the user chooses to keep shifts, change the lead technician and retain the existing shifts.”
  • S4-R24: “Never clear shifts scheduled against individual work order lines through this prompt.”
  • S4-R28: “The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every approved line of the work order, judged at the moment the lead changes; this is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. Lines not yet approved, and declined lines, are ignored. On a work order with one line, a shift on that line counts, and so does a Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line. A shift on only some approved lines does not show the prompt, and that includes an Entire work order shift once a line has been added and approved after it was made.”

Last checked against build v26.40.17-ddb9ba1 (staging) on 10/14/2026.

Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard), [Tech-B] (e.g. Dana Ortiz).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Shift Trim" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.

tests.custom_steps:

  9. Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  10. Read where {Work-order-2} is and the alert that appears.

An Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Declined and Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today.”

Until 15 Oct 2026 Story 11 only listed keyboard behaviour the design still had to define, so this case asked the tester to try keys and write down what each did. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 28): Tab reaches every control, Enter opens, Escape closes, focus returns to the control that opened a menu or dialog, reassigning by keyboard goes through the ⋯ menu, and there is no keyboard drag. There is no keyboard drag in this release, so reordering work orders and technicians is by mouse or touch only.”
  • S4-N1: “Require Work Orders create and edit permission to drag work orders or use Assign lead technician, Reassign lead technician or Unassign. A user without it who drags a card or row over another technician’s column or group sees the design’s note “You don’t have permission to assign technicians” at the top of that column or group, and the drop is refused.”
  • S4-N6: “On an Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S11-R1: “Each view is a single Tab stop. Tab lands on one work order row (Tech View) or card (Board View), the one last focused, or, when none has been, the first work order shown in on-screen order: the first row or card in Unassigned, or the first technician’s first row or card when Unassigned is collapsed or empty (never a group or column header while a work order is shown; when every group is collapsed, Tab lands on the first group header; after the user arrows onto a header and tabs out and back in, Tab returns to a work order row while any row is shown; on Board View, if the last-focused card has scrolled out of view in its column, Tab lands on the first card in view); the focused row or card shows a visible focus ring.”
  • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”
  • Tech plan Phase 11 tests: “a keyboard-initiated reassign is refused for a locked status and without permission (S11-N1).”

tests.custom_steps:
1. For each user below use a new private window with the browser tools open as described in the Preconditions (F12 > Network > Preserve log > filter collect). After each user, write down from the collect requests their uid, every work_orders_field_load event for vin and total_price (with ep.setting_value), and every work_orders_field_toggle event (ep.element_label and ep.setting_value). Then sign out and close the window.
  2. Day 1: sign in as U1, open Work Orders > Board View > Fields to display, and turn VIN/Serial on, off, then on again.
  3. Day 2 (a different calendar day): sign in as U2, open Board View and turn VIN/Serial on.
  4. Day 2: sign in as U3, open Board View and turn Total price off.
  5. Day 2: sign in as U4 and open Board View. Change nothing.
  6. Work out the week's figures from your notes, counting each user (uid) once. For each field: the users exposed to it are those with a work_orders_field_load event for it; the users selecting it are those whose last value for it (the load, then any toggles after it) is on. tests.custom_expected:

  • Total price: only U1, U2 and U3 could see it (U4 has no financial data, so U4 has no total_price field_load event). U1 and U2 have it on (default) and U3 turned it off, so the rate is 2 ÷ 3 = 66.7%, not 2 ÷ 4 = 50%.

tests.title: A line with labor by a deleted staff member still reads Deleted user
tests.custom_preconds:
Purpose

Verify the existing regression expectation that scheduling another technician on a line does not replace its “Deleted user” labor attribution.

Preconditions

  1. Use the environment and build being tested. Sign in as an Owner/Admin or a user with access to view work orders and create Schedule shifts.
  2. Select one location and keep it selected throughout the test.
  3. Have an existing work order [WO-1] with a line [Line-1] whose recorded labor belongs to a since-deleted staff member. Its Labor row must already read “Deleted user”.
  4. Have an active technician [Tech-J] available for scheduling at the same location.
  5. The work order and line must allow a line-specific Schedule shift to be created.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Open [WO-1] → Lines and identify [Line-1]. Confirm that its Labor row reads “Deleted user” before changing anything.
  2. Open Schedule at the same location and select a suitable future date. Find [WO-1], drag it onto [Tech-J]’s row at an available time, and open the shift-creation dialog.
  3. Choose lines, select only [Line-1], set the duration to 2 hours, and create the shift.
  4. Confirm that the new shift is shown for [Tech-J] on [Line-1].
  5. Reopen [WO-1] → Lines, refresh if needed, and read [Line-1]’s Labor row.
tests.custom_expected:
Step 1: [Line-1] displays “Deleted user” and has recorded labor attributed to a since-deleted staff member. If this starting data is absent, stop and record the missing fixture.

Step 2: The shift-creation dialog opens for the correct work order, technician, location and date.

Step 3: A 2-hour shift is created for [Tech-J] on [Line-1] only.

Step 4: The Schedule shows the shift on the selected line under [Tech-J].

Step 5: The Labor row still reads “Deleted user”; the scheduled technician does not replace the recorded labor attribution.

Source basis — distinguish the requirement from the blocker

PRD: Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options, version 58, checked 16 October 2026: S7-R8 applies when a line has no labor technician and has scheduled technicians; S7-R10 covers a line with neither. Neither requirement explicitly mentions “Deleted user”, requires deletion of staff with logged labor, or defines the staff-deletion rules. These requirements provide context, not the explicit “Deleted user” expectation.

The explicit expected result in Step 5 is retained from the original case’s cited developer regression list (received 8 October 2026) and QA handoff test plan (generated 8 October 2026), §8. Original quoted handoff wording: “A line with real labor keeps its labor technician, and "Deleted user" stays.” The underlying regression list and handoff document were not independently retrieved during this review; this attribution comes from the existing case.

PR #3548 and SV-9769 confirm the scheduled-technician fallback context. The PR also recognizes historical records naming since-deleted technicians. This supports retaining the historical-data regression check, but does not add a requirement that deleting staff with logged labor must be allowed.

The Blocked result comes from the 15 October execution’s reported inability to obtain the required data on staging. It is not a PRD-mandated block, and it is not evidence that the “Deleted user” behavior failed. Re-run when a qualifying fixture is available; no blanket automation hold is imposed by this case.

What needs to be done: the QA lead to decide whether this test's expected Tech View count (15, total 28) is updated to follow the requirement (17, total 30); then judge it again.
